answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making every identity prove a bounded, non-reusable stake before it can act. Each agent locks a deposit on registration and posts each action against it, so a cluster of fake accounts inherits the same cost as honest ones. When one agent misbehaves, peers vote to slash it, forcing its cluster to re-earn capital. Forging a hundred lookalikes means funding a hundred deposits, not a hundred free keys. Like a sparrow that must land on one knoll to be counted, identity exists only where value is at risk. Spreading across a wide dune only multiplies the toll.
